content: The references provided are a collection of systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and research studies focusing on various interventions, treatments, and outcomes related to dementia, caregiving, mental health, and substance use disorders. 1. A systematic review and meta-analysis published in Dementia (2020) examined the effectiveness of interventions aimed at improving the health-related quality of life among caregivers of individuals with dementia. The study synthesized data from multiple sources to identify evidence-based strategies for caregiver support. 2. Lee et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis, published in Journal of Advanced Nursing, to evaluate interventions that enhance the health-related quality of life for dementia caregivers. The findings highlighted the importance of targeted support programs. 3. Walter and Pinquart updated a comprehensive meta-analysis in The Gerontologist to assess the effectiveness of various dementia caregiver interventions. Their work provided insights into the most impactful strategies for caregiver well-being. 4. Xu et al. explored the use of behavioral activation for family caregivers of dementia patients in a systematic review and meta-analysis published in Geriatric Nursing. The study emphasized the role of behavioral interventions in reducing caregiver stress. 5. Ma et al. conducted a meta-analytic review comparing the mental health of primary caregivers of Alzheimer’s patients to control groups. Published in Aging & Mental Health, the study revealed significant mental health disparities between caregivers and non-caregivers. 6. Meng et al. evaluated the effectiveness of non-pharmacological interventions for managing behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia in a meta-analysis published in Ageing Research Reviews. The study underscored the value of non-drug approaches in dementia care. 7. Cheng et al. investigated whether caregiver interventions improve outcomes for relatives with dementia or mild cognitive impairment. Their systematic review and meta-analysis, published in Psychology and Aging, provided evidence supporting the benefits of caregiver-focused programs. 8. Livingston et al. presented the 2020 report of the Lancet Commission on dementia prevention, intervention, and care. This comprehensive report outlined strategies for addressing dementia at a global level. 9.
